lessons: Parse category names at the last underscore; instance suffixes are frame-local, not tracking identities.
Scene Z is nominal category geometry. Neither increased Z nor disappearance certifies grasp retention.
Use nominal object-center contact geometry with the supplied tool offset and minimum height; contacting only the nominal top can produce a shallow grasp.
Keep transport level and divide longer lateral transfers into a few bounded segments.
Choose release points in the observed basket frame with footprint margins; avoid fixed world-coordinate destination offsets.
A commanded release site can be reserved to reduce repeated stacking, but is not evidence of delivery.
Refresh perception after release and retreat. Bound reassociated-source attempts rather than relying on persistent object names.
Only an explicit no_collision_free_path return permits a bounded alternative route. Exceptions require stopping without changing the current gripper command.

rationale: This revision addresses the reported shallow retention, transit loss, and release-offset problems through deeper nominal contact targeting, short level transfers, basket-relative interior placement, and a retreat before fresh perception. A small exact assignment prioritizes preserving existing groups, while twelve bounded cycles allow more than six objects. Planning alternatives are restricted to explicit zero-execution rejections; uncertain execution stops the policy. Primitive completion and visual heuristics are not treated as proof of grasp or delivery.
